[spoiler= The Ancient Republic of Qartena Hadasht
[sub]An Expansion Post[/sub]]

The Republic of Qartena Hadasht is one of the oldest nations and robust cultures in the world. The residents with reference to this nation track their heritage to the twelfth century B.C. In those days the idea of Qartena Hadasht did not exist, all that existed then was the idea of the Punik peoples. These Punik peoples quickly made a name for themselves as traders. They built ships and scoured the ocean for the purpose of finding goods as well as peoples they could trade with. Their trades made them rich beyond comparison with the other native tribes on the Eastern Side of West Shamat. From there, they used their influence as well as their wealth to conquer and subjugate the tribes, as well as the lands lands near their border. This lead to numerous wars being fought in order to expand their territory, influence, and trade routes.

The most notable war fought at this expansive time was the Halmid Wars. The Halmid Wars saw the armies of the then Punik Kingdom face off against the Halmids, whom were a notable large nation adjacent to the southwestern lands of Qartena Hadasht. Numerous wars would be fought against the Halmid Menace, who would come from the tribal lands and raid Punik villages. The Halmid menace was finally vanquished under the leadership of General Abdmelqart the God-Favored. Abdmelqart the God-Favored lead the Punik Armies through numerous battles against the Halmids. Abdmelqart the God-Favored earned his nickname through the fact that he only ever lost one battle during the fourth, and last, Halmid War. The battle that he lost was when elements of his baggage train were ambushed by the high mobile Halmid tribal cavalry. The fourth Halmid war would ultimately end in the year Eight Hundred and Seventy Eight (878 B.C.) with the sacking of Helene (Hell-E-n), which was the capitol city of the Halmid peoples' nation. Helene was also the same city in which the Halmid peoples' royalty resided. Abdmelqart the God-Favored would lead the sacking of the city, as well as be the one to report his triumph to Queen Perzaphon (Purz-a-phone) who rewarded him with the Governship of the Province of Iol. The royalty of Halmids preferred death to dishonor, leaving no possibility that they could be captured by the Puniks. Later the same year, Queen Perzaphon would announce the establishment of "Ha Qartena Hadasht" or the "New City" on the ashes of what once was Helene. This would also be what established her new Kingdom of Qartena Hadasht, a kingdom where all peoples could live peacefully and trade as Punik peoples. During the construction of Qartena Hadasht, great care was taken to show off the wealth of the Punik Kingdom, and to memorialize the victories won by the Punik armies. Some of these memorials have survived to the modern day, kept safe in the halls of the Punik People's Museum. Queen Perzaphon's dynasty would last for another two hundred and sixteen years until the year Six Hundred and Sixty Two (662 B.C.) when the Punik Republic was founded. At this same time, the modern Qartenian Government system was developed. This two thousand six hundred and eighty nine year uninterrupted streak of democratic governance makes Qartena Hadasht possibly the oldest democracy in the world. It is certainly the oldest democracy on West Shamat. For over three thousands years Punik peoples have been trading, and serving to ensure that their nation remains great, and that their nation remains safe. 

It is this history which leads us to modern Qartena Hadasht, where the Suffetes sit to discuss a issue that has plagued their people for generations. The issue is with reference to expansion, and it is something that they must do. They know that stagnation will lead to the death of their Republic, and that they are outpaced by foreign rivals. When they look across the seas they see nations such as Vespurias, Hydronia, Daesun, and the Neue Republik who have all expanded to be the notable powers in their regions. Hydronia is a special case to the Qartenians, even in spite of the fact that the relationship recently has been cordial, in the fifteen hundreds, the City of Qartena was under the control of Hydronia as well as its Empire. It is a shame that they will ensure that they never relive. They knew that expansion was the only way to guarantee the safety and security of Qartena Hadasht far into the future. The only future for Qartena Hadasht is etching onto the list of the Great Powers of Erene. Through expansion, the economy has the ability to be expanded. Expansion also means that the defense industry has the ability to grow as well. Both of these things ill be key to ensuring that Qartena can stay free. The Suffetes did not arrive at this decision lightly. Records from the closed sessions of the Ha Assemblea Ha Punik reveal weeks of debate marked by frustration and quiet fear. Some warned that expansion would awaken ghosts best left buried, others argued that history had already shown the cost of hesitation. In the end, the prevailing belief was not ambition, but inevitability. To do nothing, many argued, would be to choose decline knowingly. To do nothing would be to neglect their duties to the nation, and to resign themselves to, at the least, a decade of hardship. 

Therefore, on the Morning of the thirteenth of May, twenty twenty seven. First Suffete Hanniel Magon made the decision. For the first time in nearly one hundred years, the Qartenian Military would leave its borders. One Division would be sent Northeast to secure valuable oil-rich lands along the Northeastern Coastline of West Shamat. An Army Corps sized element would be sent Northwest to secure equally as valuable natural gas rich lands that bordered the inland Sea of Purzaphon (as the Qartenians know it), as well as the Sikirski Drosdov Territories. Finally, two Army Corps would be sent south to secure a vast swath of land from the southwest shores of the Sea of Purzaphon to the northern border of Ghazr. This was the largest military operation that the Qartenians had undergone in almost two centuries, even the Qartenian Involvement in the two great wars amounted to less than this. Thankfully, it went off without a hiccup. Qartenian armor and vehicles rolled across the land to secure their objectives, and stifle any resistance from the local populous that could arise. They were perhaps a little heavy handed, although this may be true, being so far from their previous supply points was dangerous, and they would take no chances. The northern frontier would be fully occupied in two days, the south would take one week to be fully occupied by Qartenian Soldiers. They quickly worked to establish new camps in strategically important areas. They would patrol the streets, keep the locals pacified, and work to win the hearts and minds of the local communities that they now found themselves in. These soldiers were now acting more as Law Enforcement than soldiers. However, due to their pay currently being increased due to this being a deployment, many did not mind at all. 

There have been thirty five new military encampments created around the new frontier territories. These camps were given many names, some inspired by mythology, some inspired by heroes, and some inspired by the unit names themselves. The soldiers living in these camps have many duties such as the aforementioned patrolling and law enforcement duties, logistics and engineering missions, public affairs missions, surveying and construction missions, and general human aid missions. Most of these encampments were constructed rapidly, often beginning as little more than tent cities before being expanded into semi-permanent installations. A fun fact about these tent cities is that the soldiers that call them home would prank each other by throwing ants into each others camps. Progress would continue and within weeks, prefabricated barracks, command posts, maintenance yards, and medical facilities were erected to assist with the missions assigned to the soldiers. Defensive earthworks and checkpoints surrounded many of the camps, not only to protect against potential attacks, but instead to control movement along newly established supply routes. Life within the camps settled into a rigid routine, as much of Qartenian military life does. Patrol rotations were dispatched day and night, engineering units worked to improve roads and bridges, and logistics elements struggled to maintain steady supply lines across new and unfamiliar terrain. Soldiers often found themselves shifting roles depending on the needs of the area, acting as engineers one day and peacekeepers the next. Public affairs teams coordinated closely with local leaders, where local leaders existed, organizing aid distributions and attempting to explain Qartenian laws and expectations to communities that had never lived under a centralized state. The presence of the camps quickly altered the surrounding regions. Markets sprang up outside their perimeters, local laborers were hired for construction and support roles, a project to create jobs for the new citizens of Qartena, and entire communities began to orient their daily lives around the rhythms of the military. While some locals welcomed the stability and economic activity, others viewed the encampments as symbols of occupation and loss of autonomy. Tensions occasionally flared at checkpoints and during patrols, forcing commanders to balance security concerns with efforts to avoid further alienating the population. Military leaders were advised to take all actions that they could, within reason, to not provoke the locals any more than this annexation already would. For the most part, the Qartenian Government believes this was a success, despite many tragic incidents. Many of the camps were in the running to be selected by the Adirim of Defense to become permanent military installations, many soldiers enjoyed the thought that they had laid the foundation for the future of the military. At the same time, many also admitted that currently, living in the frontier was depressing. Infrastructure continued to expand, family housing was planned for key locations and long-term utility connections were laid. The moment that Qartenian soldiers began to see these types of constructions, they knew that this was their new duty station for the foreseeable future. 

Behind the initial military operation, civilian contractors with the Qartenian Government would come in. They would go between the communities and evaluate the needs of each one. They would build a massive report on the state of the new territories. These reports would be filtered back through the Qartenian Governemnt so that the communities could begin to receive the aid that they need. There were over thirty thousand of these contractors who would be going from house to house to check on things. They would be looking over the state of the roads, telephone polls, local farms and agriculture, building characteristics, and more. All of these things would have to be reported back to the Qartenian Government so that plans could be made for the purpose of future enforcement of building laws, agricultural laws, as well as to amend the Qartenian Federal Budget for the next year. Reports came into the Adirim of the Interior daily, the to-do list of the nation grew with every hour, and every inspection. Minor issues were overlooked to focus on the larger issues, small things could be left until such time that a local authority was established to handle. One of the earliest and most persistent issues faced by inspectors was the issue of language. While many Qartenians assumed the frontier populations would quickly adapt to Punik or Modern Qartenian, the reality was far more complicated. The frontier peoples are very closely related to the Qartenian peoples, many of them are the descendants of Punik peoples, but the further you traveled from Qartena, the less Punik the language became. Translators were in short supply, given that the languages spoken were not of any nation, but of peoples previously left unbothered by civilization, and misunderstandings became common. In some communities, entire inspections were conducted through hand gestures, hastily written notes, or local intermediaries whose loyalties were uncertain. Several early disputes that escalated into violence were later determined to have begun as simple failures to communicate.

Many of these communities had been without an established national authority for quite some time, in some cases for generations, and some had never had a internationally recognized government. While a number of towns and villages had developed their own local authorities to keep the peace, whether it is a councils of elders, merchant leagues, or informal militias, others had descended into lawlessness, governed only by force, violence, reputation, and fear. It was this situation that the Qartenian Military Police and Gendarmes entered into, tasked with restoring order and asserting the authority of the Republic where none had existed before. Their role varied from place to place. In communities willing to cooperate, they acted primarily as peacekeepers, tasked with mediating disputes, separating rival groups, and providing a visible but restrained presence meant to reassure rather than intimidate. In other areas, however, they were forced into the role of peace enforcers, imposing curfews, conducting weapons seizures, and carrying out raids against armed groups that refused to recognize Qartenian authority. Which role they assumed was often determined less by doctrine than by the reactions of the local population, and by how violently those populations chose to resist their new overlords. They would not be caught off guard, and they would not be taken advantage of. In some settlements, Qartenian forces encountered organized criminal groups that had filled the power vacuum left by the absence of a state. These groups controlled trade routes, extorted the local population, and enforced their will on terrified civilians. In such cases, the response was decisive. Suspected leaders were detained, compounds were raided, searched, and those identified as culpable were arrested and removed from the region entirely. To many locals, these actions were welcomed, even if they feared what would come next. Elsewhere, the situation was far more complex. Entire communities were found to be deeply complicit in corruption and violence, with criminal authority had begun to govern everyday life. In these areas, resistance to Qartenian inspectors and soldiers was widespread and often coordinated. Patrols were ambushed, inspections obstructed, and warnings ignored. Confrontations escalated quickly, and in several instances resulted in sustained firefights between civilians and Qartenian forces. A number of civilians were killed in these engagements, their deaths officially recorded as the tragic but unavoidable consequence of restoring order in a hostile territory. In many cases, when civilians attempted to block Qartenian inspectors or soldiers from entering their land, viewing the inspections as an intrusion or a prelude to dispossession, the Qartenian Law Enforcement would detain them and attempt to ascertain the issue. Typically these issues would begin as shouting matches and standoffs, they would sometimes devolve into violence when weapons were drawn or stones were thrown. These moments, brief and chaotic, often ended with irreversible consequences. Investigations would follow, reports would be filed, and the Republic would move on, but for the communities involved, the cost was immediate and personal. By the end of the first few months of occupation, order had been imposed across most of the frontier, it was accepted in some places, feared in others, and resented in many. 

Qartenian Soldiers and Law Enforcement would affect around five thousands (5,000) arrests within the first month of occupying the new "frontier area." These arrests were for a variety of reasons. The soldiers and law enforcement officers were instructed to be lenient and do their best to not step on the locals' toes. Low level violations and misdemeanors would be overlooked, or punished with simple court appearances. However, the more severe violations of the law are still met with arrest, detention, and in some cases transportation to the mainland of Qartena Hadasht for access to more high level courts and detention facilities. In these same months, there were over fifty five Law Enforcement involved shootings in the frontier territories. Twenty five of these shootings ended in fatalities. Twenty eight individuals were shot and killed by Qartenian Military and Law Enforcement while three Qartenian Law Enforcement Officers were killed in the line of duty during this time. The number of violent incidents involving Military and Law Enforcement were concerning to the Government. Following these incidents the Qartenian Military and Law Enforcement patrolling the new territories would adopt new tactics to attempt to deescalate incidents, and attempting to stay back further in incidents involving gunfire. These type of violent incidents are less frequent now, but even still, violent incidents still occur at a higher rate than the mainland territories. 

With Qartenian Law Enforcement also came Qartenian Emergency Management. The first few months immediately see the establishment of radio towers, the Government seizure of established Fire Departments, Ambulance Stations, Police Stations, Hospitals, Utility Depots, and more. All of these things would be the first line of defense for the new citizens of their Republic. Within a week some of the areas near the border were already operating on the Qartenian Emergency Management system. Listening to their radio communications became a national sensation for the first week that the first Police and Fire Departments were operating in the new frontier territories. In many places, Law Enforcement Officers, Firefighters, Paramedics, and utility workers were allowed to keep their positions if they could pass a skills test put on by the the Qartenian Emergency Management Standards and Training Division. Those who failed were put on probation and not allowed to perform their duties until they can pass the academy for their discipline of service. Those who pass are eligible to apply for a fast-track certification for their discipline of service, but they will have to obtain certifications for their discipline of service while they continue their service. One of the first things that the new Adirim of Emergency Management had to do was establish regional emergency communication centers. These would work with the Adirim of Labor and the Adirim of the Interior to create jobs for people in the Frontier Territories. There would have to be more than twelve thousand dispatchers for all of the new area in the Republic. That doesn't count the number of Law Enforcement, Firefighters, Doctors, Paramedics, Emergency Medical Technicians, and more that would have to be hired as well. Following that detailed maps would have to be created addresses logged, and equipment purchased. These things would have to be done quickly, as emergencies do not stop. A two year plan has been created by the Adirim of Emergency Management to move the Qartenian Military into their camps and replace their Law Enforcement duties with local Law Enforcement and Federal Gendarmes. 

As all of this what happening, a third group was looking to benefit from the growth of Qartena's borders. The private sector was also sending in their surveyors. These were rich lands, rich with oil, rich with natural gas, rich with coal and iron. These lands promised to bring massive gains to whichever company could buy the land first. Many companies would send in their surveyors, lawyers, and negotiators to attempt to get first bid on the rights to the resources that many people did not know existed directly under their land, and has for centuries. The issue was so bad, and so predatory that the Qartenian Government would have to pass new laws over the exploitation of these people by Qartenian Companies. However, the Government of Qartena was not the only "regulating body." As previously mentioned, the problem of violence in the frontier areas was great. There are numerous reports of aggravated locals, who had been taken advantage of by Qartenian Companies, hunting down and attacking those which had "robbed" them. This of course, only lead to more issues in the frontier areas, although the former was true, the development of the frontier areas was carrying on at a rapid pace. New oil rigs, refineries, coal mines, farms, and more went up every single day. The economy of Qartena was being fed a diet of nearly two times the natural resources that it previously had. This expansion would make Qartena Hadasht one of the largest oil producing nations in the world. It would also put Qartena Hadasht in the running as one of the largest energy producing nations in the world. This could work to make some nations dependent on Qartenian exports. This is at least what the Government is hoping to achieve. Nations dependent on what Qartena Hadasht can offer means that those nations will not be in the position to attack it, and they will be in the position that they can be influenced. It's a strange game that the Government will have to play, but when you play from a position of disadvantage, you have to be crafty. 

The legal representation of individuals against predatory Qartenian Companies lead to another pressing issue, the naturalization of the seventy-five million people who were now within Qartenian borders. This was a daunting issue which overwhelmed existing Qartenian Border Administration. The Qartenian Border Administration, who up until that point had just been operating the nation's ports of entry,  as well as processing travel and immigration paperwork, now had seventy five million people who required naturalization into the Republic of Qartena Hadasht. Because of the fact that this issue was so vast in scale, the new Adirim of Naturalization was founded. The Adirim of Naturalization would meet with up to two thousand five hundred people a day to establish their citizenship in offices all across the new frontiers. This process took an enormous amount of time, and especially, a lot of patience. These people hadn't asked to become citizens of Qartena Hadasht. Some of them didn't even want to become citizens of Qartena Hadasht, deciding to instead take the Government assistance to leave the nation and resettle outside the boundaries of the nation, or take the opportunity to attempt to relocate to a third nation. But, in the end, as mentioned there were seventy five million new citizens for the Republic of Qartena Hadasht. This vastly increased the amount of money that the Government was going to have to spend on social programs as the frontier areas were caught up to the level that the mainland. This new spending allocation will hit the national budget hard for some years, it is already expected that the nation will have to dip into its' Sovereign Wealth Fund to fund them for the next decade. But following the decade, when these lands have been integrated, the new businesses moved in, and the people employed by Qartenian companies, the profits would eventually vastly outnumber the losses. 

Next up was the business of establishing political representation within these frontier communities. Many areas would be allowed to keep the locally elected authorities that they had, provided they were aligned with the values of the Qartenian Constitution. However, some local authorities had to be scrapped completely, in the event that they even existed. In these communities, local overseers were appointed by the Government to ready the communities for elections. These overseers were tasked with the enormous responsibility of readying people for one of the most consequential elections of their lives. They were required to catalog existing power structures, mediate disputes between rival local factions, and determine whether former leaders could be trusted to participate in the new system. In many cases, individuals who had ruled by force or informal authority attempted to legitimize themselves by presenting as democratic leaders. Others, fearful of losing power, actively undermined the process through intimidation or misinformation. Political campaigning was everywhere in these communities, showering the locals with social, political, and economic issues that, in some cases, did not even apply to them a month ago. Campaign posters appeared overnight on buildings that had never hosted public notices before. Loudspeakers broadcast promises of representation, stability, and prosperity to populations that were still adjusting to the presence of Qartenian patrols in their streets. Many people reported being absolutely overwhelmed, unsure whether participation would protect them or expose them to retaliation from neighbors or former power brokers. Over the next few months, municipalities were incorporated, local elections were held, and new regional governments were set up. Voter turnout varied widely. Some communities embraced the opportunity with enthusiasm, while others participated reluctantly or not at all. In several cases, elections had to be delayed or repeated due to security concerns, allegations of coercion, or disputes over voter eligibility. Each level of government proved vitally important to ensuring that the Qartenian Government system functioned properly, but the speed at which these structures were introduced strained both administrators and citizens. Some individuals took the opportunity to establish entirely new political parties, often built around local identity, economic grievances, or opposition to Qartenian influence. Others aligned themselves with existing mainland parties, hoping to secure funding, protection, or future advancement within the broader political system of the Republic.

Reactions were mixed on the home front, in the mainland of Qartena there were many people who were for and against this occupation. Many believed that this would create a strain on the economy, and that the short term impacts on the economy are going to be an extreme issue. This is a problem that was echoed across of Qartena. At the same time, however, many people were praising the Government for having identified these new resource rich lands for expansion. You'd be right to assume that this became the major political talking point within the nation. The point of contention wasn't that the Government was annexing the land, but what should happen to the people who live there, and what should happen to the companies that were expanding there. Many people did not believe that the civilians living in the frontier territories should be given citizenship as fast as it was happening. The issue was so contentious that there were even protests in front of the Punik House, where the Ha Assemblea Ha Punik (The Punik Assembly), Qartena's legislature meets. Their protests were not effective in changing the opinion of the legislatures. Another issue which drew major backlash was the Qartenian companies that "preyed" on the civilians in the frontier territories. Many civilians were targeted and signed away the mineral rights of their land for promises of future employment, fast tracked citizenship, and more. These promises skewed the perception of these peoples on the agreement that they were signing, and many believe were illegal under Qartenian law. These cases are still ongoing, and many people were impacted by these predatory agreements. For many frontier families, land ownership was not understood in legal terms at all. Some of these peoples have not had land laws for sometime, some didn't have laws governing their actions at all. Fields, homes, and grazing lands were often passed down without written deeds, meaning that some people couldn't prove ownership of their own land. When Qartenian legal frameworks were applied to these lands, many residents struggled to understand how something held by generations could be signed away in a single afternoon. Some individuals also turned to forging documents, or even claiming ownership of land that was not theirs. many disputes were started because of the issue of land. Qartenian officials would later note that resistance was often strongest not where resources were richest, but where familiar ties and disputes ran deepest. Many other issues related to the annexation of these lands were also being discussed, and remain a topic of heated discussion at this time. 

All of these developments and changes have turned the lives of those who lived in these frontier territories upside down. Life will never look the same in these areas as it did before the Qartenians arrived. There will always be arguments about whether life was better with or without Qartenian involvement. Its possible that some may even be driven to the point of violent action against the Qartenian government. There are many unknowns for what the future looks like, not only for the people of this land, but also for the nation that they now call home as well. These unknowns will, as they always do, become known in time. But for now, they will be immersed one day at a time into a new culture and way of life that they are wholly unfamiliar with. Eventually, at some point, it will become a way of life that becomes normal for them. Something that the Qartenian Government one day hopes that they will enjoy, and find the ability to be contempt with. It's really the only path forwards now. Unless a foreign nation comes in and takes the land by force, or they manage to win their freedom through violence, they will be Qartena Hadasht citizens and their kids will be Qartena Hadasht citizens until the collapse of the nation. Time marches on. 

[/spoiler]

[quote=greater_rostoria;60983167][spoiler=[b]Corporate Withdrawal: Erene 2000[/b]]

The Zaibatsu, four conglomerates originating from UREV, discussed recent developments in their shared Valdderan economic project, and concerning information regarding the government's violation of their shared contract. The Zaibatsu learned that the Valdderan government was planning on violating and minimising Zaibatsu control over the economy, directly going against the terms of the contract and the interests of the Zaibatsu. It had become clear to them, Valddera was no longer a trustworthy entity to operate in.

Corporate security forces from the Antonio Consortium and Terran Industries were quickly mobilised towards key businesses and infrastructure; corporate headquarters, factory complexes, power & water stations, or even entertainment buildings stadiums and television sets. The corporate security proudly displayed their weapons among the cities of the nation, large divisions of corporate soldiers were brought in and given full permission by the Valdderan government to operate in the nation, initially to combat antigovernmental forces then to maintain stability in the war torn regions. Local police were confronted by corporate owned APCs and equipped troops, losing control over the situation around corporate controlled property and assets.

Once security was guaranteed, the corporations began mass-selling all the subsidiary businesses that were bought, selling them at the same price they were purchased for to other foreign corporations or even governments, including the Valdderan one. Large sectors of the Valdderan economy shut down the Zaibatsu stopped operations and went into overtime to remove all assets which would be sent back to UREV. Thousands of people would find themselves jobless as their place of work shut down and went into listing, while the corporations took their money and property, loading them onto large cargo and freight ships to be shipped back home.

The Antonio Consortium was given a large monopoly on the water and power sector, given permission to rebuild utilities following the war with Daesun. Once they began their operation, all power and water stations were shutdown all at once, large populations instantly lost access to their utilities and many operating them were let go as the consortium wasn't planning on restarting the stations. Power and water stations which were built by the Antonio Consortium were demolish using controlled explosives or demolition vehicles, while stations that were instead bought had any moveable assets removed but otherwise were left untouched. The Antonio Consortium demolished any factories they had built while untouched those they bought, and power lines were severed to slow down any efforts to bring them back up. Factories which weren't demolished were sold off as quickly as possible. The stadium which Antonio bought ceased their renovations mid-way through, leaving the scaffolding as was and removing any assets they could, though the stadium and football team werent sold off and instead kept while the consortium made up their mind.

Terran Industries did the same, demolishing factories they built and instantly letting go thousands of local workers leading to a massive increase in unemployment in some areas reliant on manufacturing. Unfinished or unsold cars, their frames, or even as simple as headlights were marked as corporate property and shipped off towards cargo vessels to be sent to UREV, while production lines were sabotaged or entire complexes sold off as quickly as possible to other corporations such as Lagonda. Machinery produced or bought was also moved out of the country, leaving many factories as large empty husks with random parts or unmaintained machinery scattered around. Company vehicles were hurriedly shipped out of the country or sent into scrapyards to be quickly destroyed, while those very same scrapyards, owned by Antonio Consortium or Amery, were listed off to other entities.
